OPERATOR_TOOL_CONTRACT_ADDITIONS.OT-1_at_run_time: Unchanged: each tool refuses if its own directory has a .git ancestor (measured on the real tools).
OPERATOR_TOOL_CONTRACT_ADDITIONS.OT-14: Unchanged: the mint's operator principal is the OEP-1-observed one.
OPERATOR_TOOL_CONTRACT_ADDITIONS.OT-15: Only the SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier is sent; the plaintext derives it and goes to the depositor stdin only (harness VERIFIER_ONLY + PLAINTEXT_NEVER_SENT).
OPERATOR_TOOL_CONTRACT_ADDITIONS.OT-16: Startup closed and session bound: no query/fragment; exact host, port, database; driver from explicit options (harness STARTUP_CLOSED + refusal scenarios).
OPERATOR_TOOL_CONTRACT_ADDITIONS.OT-17: Driver bound by content: the digest of its files equals --driver-digest before load.
OPERATOR_TOOL_CONTRACT_ADDITIONS.OT-18: Server authenticated (owner AC-8): --ca-file must hash to --ca-sha256 and hold exactly one CA certificate; it is passed as the ONLY `ca` (the system store is not consulted), with rejectUnauthorized true, servername = the target host, minVersion TLSv1.2 and tls.checkServerIdentity; nothing is downloaded. Measured on real TLS with the real postgres.js (tests/custody/d1-tls-trust.test.ts) and on the pinned tools under both harnesses (TLS_VERIFY_FULL_PINNED, REFUSES_CA_MISSING, REFUSES_CA_MODIFIED).
OPERATOR_TOOL_CONTRACT_ADDITIONS.OT-19: Each tool refuses to work when a variable matching ^(PG[A-Z0-9_]*|NODE_OPTIONS|NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED|NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS|SSL_CERT_FILE|SSL_CERT_DIR|OPENSSL_CONF|OPENSSL_MODULES)$ (case-insensitive) is in its environment (harness REFUSES_AMBIENT_PG_ENV). NODE_OPTIONS acts before the tool runs: the launcher allowlist is what keeps it out; OT-19 is defence in depth.

OEP1_PROBE_CONTRACT.central_invariant: PLAINTEXT_PASSWORD_SERVER_EXPOSURE = IMPOSSIBLE_BY_CONSTRUCTION. OEP-1 no longer asks a server whether it would log the plaintext: the plaintext never reaches it. The probe proves the SESSION the mint will use.

what_the_probe_proves.TARGET_SESSION_BOUND: current_user = session_user = the operator principal; current_database() = the route-B database; server_version_num >= 100000 (SCRAM verifiers accepted) — observed inside the session on the N04 host and route-B port the tool bound.
what_the_probe_proves.STARTUP_PARAMETERS_CLOSED: the settings whose source is 'client' are EXACTLY the measured postgres.js 3.4.9 set (application_name=postgres.js, client_encoding=UTF8): no startup GUC rode in.
what_the_probe_proves.PROBE_MINT_CONFIGURATION_COHERENT: R3: the connection the probe OBSERVED -- the host, port, database and user it bound, the TLS session its verification accepted (verified, the peer certificate fingerprint and the anchor its chain reached) and the digest of the driver files it loaded -- equals what the mint will use: the N04 host, route-B port and database, the principal the evidence records (= current_user = session_user), the pinned project certificate as anchor, the pinned driver digest. The session fingerprint is recomputed from the OBSERVED values. No term compares a repository constant with itself.

OEP1_PROBE_CONTRACT.what_it_no_longer_infers: Whether any logging setting, extension, hook or lock wait would record the PLAINTEXT. That class is open (the recertification's finding) and is closed by construction instead.
OEP1_PROBE_CONTRACT.derived_material_exposure: Informational classification of whether the VERIFIER could be logged (POSSIBLE / NOT_INDICATED / UNKNOWN; never 'absent'). It gates nothing about the plaintext and is never merged with PLAINTEXT_NOT_PRESENT.

statements.IDENTITY: SELECT current_user AS current_user_name, session_user AS session_user_name, current_database() AS database_name, current_setting('server_version_num') AS server_version_num
statements.CLIENT_SETTINGS: SELECT name, setting FROM pg_catalog.pg_settings WHERE source = 'client' ORDER BY name
statements.DERIVED_MATERIAL_SETTINGS: SELECT name, setting, source FROM pg_catalog.pg_settings WHERE name = ANY($1::text[]) ORDER BY name

OEP1_PROBE_CONTRACT.transaction: ONE, BEGIN READ ONLY; the derived list is the only bound parameter; nothing through unsafe().
OEP1_PROBE_CONTRACT.probe_contract_clauses: PC-1..PC-6 in scripts/custody/d1-oep1-probe-harness.ts (measured on the real probe tool v2).
OEP1_PROBE_CONTRACT.output_line: probe: OBSERVED, identity, client_settings, derived_settings, connection {host, port, database, user, tls {verified, peer_sha256, anchor_sha256}, driver_digest}

OEP1_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT.path: docs/ops/release/FIBDB053_D1_AUDITOR_OEP1_EVIDENCE_v<semver>.json (append-only; an explicit CHAIN, not "the highest version wins")
required_fields: verdict (CLOSED only when every gating sub-verdict is PASS)
predecessor (null for the first record, else the path of the record it follows)
acknowledged_non_closed [{path, resolution}] (exactly the earlier records whose verdict is not CLOSED)
OEP1_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT.recomputation: PMR-14 RECOMPUTES every sub-verdict and the derived classification from the observation and the repository (never trusts the record); a consistent non-PASS record does not close OEP-1 (recertification survivor E1).
invalidation_predicates: IP-1: any CHANNEL_BINDING pin differs from the evidence's hashes.
IP-2: N04's host, the route-B port or database differ from the evidence's.
IP-3: the mint's operator URL names another principal (launcher OC-4 and mint OT-14 refuse).
IP-4: observed_at_utc is not before the effective N08.
IP-5: a later OEP-1 evidence record exists on the chain (it becomes the head and must itself close OEP-1 and acknowledge every earlier non-CLOSED record).
IP-6: the channel certification event is not a terminal PASS for an ancestor carrying the same effective CHANNEL_BINDING.
IP-7: the driver digest differs from the repository's.
IP-8: the pinned trust root (CHANNEL_BINDING.tls) differs from the anchor the evidence observed.

chain.rule: Every OEP-1 evidence file is one link of ONE linear chain: exactly one root (predecessor null); every other record names an existing record of a LOWER version; no two records name the same predecessor; every file is on the chain that ends at the head. The HEAD is evaluated, and it must acknowledge, each with a non-empty resolution, exactly the earlier records whose verdict is not CLOSED. A later PASS therefore never erases an earlier FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE: it has to name it.
chain.residual: The rules read the files present in the tree. A record deleted from history before a later one is written is not seen by them; the independent certifier reads the history (git log of the evidence paths) as part of certifying a PHASE 2 candidate.

TLS_TRUST_POLICY.trust_root: The exact project certificate downloaded from the Supabase dashboard for bvyzblhqymxruxdguaee: CN=Supabase Root 2021 CA (2021-04-28 .. 2031-04-26), raw sha256 7007235814..., DER sha256 807025ad50..., SPKI sha256 ba33264923...; byte-identical to the 2021 production root the official Supabase CLI embeds, NOT the same-DN 2025 root (different key) nor the staging root.
TLS_TRUST_POLICY.measured: On real TLS with the real postgres.js 3.4.9: the pinned CA + the right host -> the server is reached and the password is sent once, after authentication; another CA, another host name, an expired or a self-signed certificate -> rejected before any startup message, zero passwords; ssl require -> an impostor with another CA receives the cleartext password (the recertification finding reproduced).
TLS_TRUST_POLICY.what_remains: postgres.js 3.4.9 still offers no SCRAM channel binding and still answers a cleartext-password request; with the server authenticated only the real server can ask. The CA expires 2031-04-26; a rotation is a new owner decision and a new channel.
